newsitem.title: UK: Physical aluminium and copper still slow in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Physical aluminium and copper still slow in Europe.

text.p: Premiums and discounts for physical aluminium and copper are holding at stable levels in Europe, although business is running at a fairly low ebb, traders said.

In aluminium, interest and activity appears to be centred on the other main areas - the U.S. and the Far East. Meanwhile, the copper market is finely balanced at present, so there is little pressure on premiums.
Aluminium traders said the magnet-like attraction of strong spot premiums in the U.S. continues to draw Russian metal out of locations such as the U.K. and Helsingborg.
But with sizeable tonnages having moved across the Atlantic already, the really high premiums in excess of seven cents/lb are not attainable any more.
In the Far East, premiums for Russian metal are nearing $80, while Western levels are in the mid-$80s and showing signs of reaching $90, they said.
Copper traders said there has been little in the way of active consumer or merchant business, with the market marking time.
Much-mooted Chinese buying has yet to materialise in any significant size, with recent parcels largely around the 500-tonne level.
Some said Friday's shipment of some 6,000 tonnes of copper from the LME's Singapore warehouse could well be the start of a sustained outflow.
Others thought the Chinese were still holding off and waiting for lower prices.
"Unless they really have to buy, it would be more logical to hold off until later in the year when stocks will be building up," one merchant source said.
